name: base64 0.23 (Simd engine)
baseline: base64's scalar GeneralPurpose engine (general_purpose::STANDARD, the only engine through 0.22 and still the prelude default in 0.23)
verdict_reason: The default base64 crate gained SIMD engines in 0.23.0 (2026-07-23). Its PR measured 3.7x-3.8x faster encoding and 6.5x-7.1x faster decoding than the scalar engine on AVX2, with instruction counts down 4.7x-7.1x. The speedup is opt-in: STANDARD and the prelude constants are still scalar, so callers must construct engine::Simd.
tier_reason: First-party PR numbers from public criterion and Callgrind benchmarks; the machine is only described as AVX2, x86-64-v3.
workload: encode_slice and decode_slice into existing buffers, 3 KiB and 3 MiB inputs, STANDARD alphabet.
hardware: x86-64-v3 machine with AVX2 (model not stated)
platforms: x86_64 AVX2 and aarch64 NEON; runtime detection (Simd) needs std; Avx2/Neon engines work in no_std; scalar fallback elsewhere
install: cargo add base64 (0.23 or later), then use base64::engine::Simd
one_liner: The base64 crate's own SIMD engine (0.23+): 3.7x faster encode and up to 7.1x faster decode than its scalar engine, if you opt in.
how_it_is_fast: Implements Wojciech Muła's vectorized base64 algorithms: AVX2 uses a multiply-based bit interleave, NEON a shift/mask variant, both with shared lookup tables. The Simd engine detects AVX2 or NEON at runtime and falls back to the scalar kernels for tails and unsupported CPUs.
use_it_when: You already depend on base64 and encode or decode more than a few hundred bytes at a time
x86_64 with AVX2 or any aarch64 target
You want SIMD speed without adding base64-simd as another dependency
skip_it_when: Custom alphabets: only STANDARD and URL_SAFE are accelerated
Crates that must stay #![forbid(unsafe_code)]: disable the default simd-unsafe feature
Secret material: the crate documents its GeneralPurpose engine as not constant-time and offers no constant-time SIMD engine
caveats: First-party numbers on an unnamed machine; no third-party run yet
Only 3 KiB and 3 MiB inputs were measured; short inputs may gain less
Wall-clock and instruction counts are from the PR description, not a published report
tradeoffs: The simd-unsafe feature (on by default) is the crate's only use of unsafe
Opt-in API: existing code using STANDARD sees no change

evidence.quote: times with the criterion benchmarks (AVX2, x86-64-v3, this machine):
Added SIMD-accelerated engines behind the default-on `simd-unsafe` feature
